accepted.s: How many new high-yielding field-crop varieties were released by ICAR during 2019–21?
accepted.x: ICAR released 562 new high-yielding field-crop varieties during 2019–21.
accepted.tq: Use the precise year-period and distinguish it from other variety-release figures.
accepted.sec: Seeds - HYVs, ICAR releases, SRR, seed village, PPVFR, GM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the climate-resilient varieties released in January 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Climate-resilient varieties of 25 crops were released.
2. A total of 3,236 high-yielding varieties had been notified since 2014.
3. The number of high-yielding varieties notified during 1969–2014 was 3,969.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Climate-resilient varieties of 25 crops were released in January 2026, while 3,236 HYVs had been notified since 2014 compared with 3,969 during 1969–2014.
accepted.tq: Group closely related numerical facts and verify each statement independently.
accepted.sec: Seeds - HYVs, ICAR releases, SRR, seed village, PPVFR, GM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes Seed Replacement Rate from Varietal Replacement Rate?
o: SRR concerns only genetically modified seed, whereas VRR concerns organic seed.
SRR concerns varieties released during the last three to five years, whereas VRR concerns certified seed.
SRR concerns certified or quality seed, whereas VRR concerns varieties released during the last three to five years.
SRR measures seed exports, whereas VRR measures seed imports.
accepted.x: SRR is the percentage of crop area sown with certified or quality seed. VRR is the percentage of area under varieties released in the preceding three to five years.
accepted.tq: Separate two similar abbreviations by matching each with its defining measure.
accepted.sec: Seeds - HYVs, ICAR releases, SRR, seed village, PPVFR, GM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principal purpose of a Seed Village programme is to provide farmers with:
o: Foundation seed for local production of certified seed
Farm machinery for processing harvested seed
accepted.x: Under the Seed Village approach, farmers receive foundation seed and produce certified seed locally.
accepted.tq: Identify the programme by its operational mechanism rather than by its broad objective.
accepted.sec: Seeds - HYVs, ICAR releases, SRR, seed village, PPVFR, GM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Act, 2001:
1. It established the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Authority.
2. Farmers may save, use, exchange and sell farm-saved seed.
3. Such farm-saved seed may be sold as branded seed.
4. Terminator or GURT seeds are banned.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. Farmers may sell farm-saved seed only as unbranded seed; therefore statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Find the single reversed qualification in an otherwise familiar legal provision.
accepted.sec: Seeds - HYVs, ICAR releases, SRR, seed village, PPVFR, GM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Seeds Act, 1966 — Regulation of quality of notified seeds
PPV&FR Act, 2001 — Approval of all GM crops
Environment Protection Act, 1986 — Farmers’ right to sell branded farm-saved seed
Seeds Act, 1966 — Ban on all genome-edited crops
accepted.x: The Seeds Act, 1966 regulates the quality of notified seeds. The PPV&FR Act protects breeders and farmers’ seed-related rights, while GM approvals are handled under the specified environmental regulatory framework.
accepted.tq: Match each statute with its specific regulatory subject and reject swapped authorities.
accepted.sec: Seeds - HYVs, ICAR releases, SRR, seed village, PPVFR, GM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the only commercially approved genetically modified crop in India, according to the stated status?
accepted.x: Bt cotton, approved in 2002, is the only commercially approved GM crop. GM mustard and Bt brinjal have not been cleared for commercial cultivation.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among closely related crops by their approval status and year.
accepted.sec: Seeds - HYVs, ICAR releases, SRR, seed village, PPVFR, GM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about GM crop regulation in India:
1. GEAC functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
2. Its regulatory framework is linked to the Environment Protection Act, 1986 and Rules of 1989.
3. GM mustard DMH-11 was cleared by GEAC in 2022 but remains under Supreme Court scrutiny.
4. Bt brinjal has been commercially cleared.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Bt brinjal has not been cleared, so statement 4 is false.
accepted.tq: Identify the wrong regulatory-status statement while retaining the correct authority and legal basis.
accepted.sec: Seeds - HYVs, ICAR releases, SRR, seed village, PPVFR, GM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The genome-edited rice variety DRR Dhan 100 Kamala was developed from which variety?
accepted.x: DRR Dhan 100 Kamala was developed from Samba Mahsuri. Pusa DST Rice 1 was developed from MTU1010.
accepted.tq: Separate two genome-edited varieties by identifying their respective parent varieties.
accepted.sec: Seeds - HYVs, ICAR releases, SRR, seed village, PPVFR, GM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the genome-edited rice varieties announced in May 2025 is correct?
o: SDN-1 edits introduce foreign DNA and therefore necessarily follow all GMO rules.
Pusa DST Rice 1 was developed from MTU1010 and is due for commercial launch.
DRR Dhan 100 Kamala was developed from Bt cotton and has already been commercially launched.
Both varieties are conventional GM crops cleared for commercial cultivation in 2002.
accepted.x: Pusa DST Rice 1 was developed from MTU1010 and was due for commercial launch. SDN-1 edits carry no foreign DNA and therefore bypass GMO rules as stated.
accepted.tq: Test the exact parentage, launch status and regulatory distinction in one precise option.
accepted.sec: Seeds - HYVs, ICAR releases, SRR, seed village, PPVFR, GM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In January 2026, ICAR released 184 varieties of 25 crops. Which one of the following correctly represents the stated composition?
o: 124 cereals and 22 cotton varieties, including 24 Bt cotton varieties
122 cotton and 24 cereal varieties, including 22 Bt cotton varieties
184 cereals, of which 25 were Bt cotton varieties
122 cereals and 24 cotton varieties, including 22 Bt cotton varieties
accepted.x: The release comprised 122 cereal varieties and 24 cotton varieties, including 22 Bt cotton varieties.
accepted.tq: Split the aggregate figure into its component figures and reject reversed categories.
accepted.sec: Seeds - HYVs, ICAR releases, SRR, seed village, PPVFR, GM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: As stated for May 2026, the National Agricultural Research System had released how many climate-resilient varieties?
accepted.x: The National Agricultural Research System had released 2,996 climate-resilient varieties as stated for May 2026.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the NARS figure from the separate HYV notification and ICAR release figures.
accepted.sec: Seeds - HYVs, ICAR releases, SRR, seed village, PPVFR, GM status  [APPSC]

accepted.s: What is the principal biological function of earthworms in vermicomposting?
o: They eliminate the need for all soil testing.
They convert green manure crops into seed varieties.
They convert chemical fertilisers into pesticides.
They convert organic waste into rich manure.
accepted.x: In vermicomposting, earthworms convert organic waste into nutrient-rich manure.
accepted.tq: Apply the process definition to identify the actual function of the organism.
accepted.sec: Organic and natural inputs - vermicompost, green manure, NPOP, PKVY, ZBNF, APCNF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a green manure crop mentioned in relation to agricultural inputs?
accepted.x: Sunn hemp, dhaincha and green gram are mentioned in connection with green manure seed. Bt cotton is a genetically modified crop and is not a green manure crop.
accepted.tq: Find the odd item by classifying each crop according to its agricultural use.
accepted.sec: Organic and natural inputs - vermicompost, green manure, NPOP, PKVY, ZBNF, APCNF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: For Kharif 2026, Andhra Pradesh set aside what amount for green manure seed?
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh set aside ₹62.20 crore for green manure seed for Kharif 2026.
accepted.tq: Use the expenditure figure rather than confusing it with fertiliser or seed-subsidy amounts.
accepted.sec: Organic and natural inputs - vermicompost, green manure, NPOP, PKVY, ZBNF, APCNF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The quantity of green manure seed provided for Kharif 2026 included which of the following?
o: 91,918 quintals of sunn hemp, dhaincha and green gram
7.46 lakh quintals of sunn hemp alone
41.70 lakh quintals of dhaincha and green gram
91,918 tonnes of cotton and rice seed
accepted.x: The stated quantity was 91,918 quintals comprising sunn hemp, dhaincha and green gram seed.
accepted.tq: Check both the unit and the crop composition before selecting the quantitative answer.
accepted.sec: Organic and natural inputs - vermicompost, green manure, NPOP, PKVY, ZBNF, APCNF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the National Programme for Organic Production (NPOP)?
o: It is a fertiliser-consumption monitoring programme of Andhra Pradesh.
It was launched in 2001 under the Commerce Ministry through APEDA.
It was launched in 2015 by the Ministry of Environment and Forests as a natural-farming mission.
It is implemented exclusively by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha.
accepted.x: NPOP is the National Programme for Organic Production, established in 2001 under the Commerce Ministry through APEDA.
accepted.tq: Use the ministry-and-agency pairing to avoid a department swap.
accepted.sec: Organic and natural inputs - vermicompost, green manure, NPOP, PKVY, ZBNF, APCNF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which certification route is described as an alternative to NPOP for organic production?
accepted.x: PGS-India is the alternative certification route mentioned alongside NPOP for organic production.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between certification systems and unrelated agricultural regulatory platforms.
accepted.sec: Organic and natural inputs - vermicompost, green manure, NPOP, PKVY, ZBNF, APCNF  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY):
1. It promotes cluster-based organic farming.
2. Each cluster consists of 50 farmers and 50 acres.
3. Certification may be through PGS-India or NPOP.
4. Two hundred new clusters were added in the tribal areas of Visakhapatnam.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly describe PKVY as presented: its cluster structure, certification routes and the addition of 200 tribal-area clusters in Visakhapatnam.
accepted.tq: Confirm a complete set of scheme features rather than selecting only the most familiar pair.
accepted.sec: Organic and natural inputs - vermicompost, green manure, NPOP, PKVY, ZBNF, APCNF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Zero Budget Natural Farming was developed by:
o: The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Authority
accepted.x: Zero Budget Natural Farming was developed by Subhash Palekar.
accepted.tq: Match the farming approach with its named proponent, not its implementing organisation.
accepted.sec: Organic and natural inputs - vermicompost, green manure, NPOP, PKVY, ZBNF, APCNF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Andhra Pradesh Community Managed Natural Farming (APCNF)?
o: It is run by RySS and uses jeevamrutham and ghanajeevamrutham.
It is run by APEDA and uses only imported chemical fertilisers.
It is run by GEAC and regulates commercial GM crops.
It is run by NARS and releases climate-resilient seed varieties.
accepted.x: APCNF is run by Rythu Sadhikara Samstha (RySS) and uses jeevamrutham and ghanajeevamrutham.
accepted.tq: Identify the implementing body and the characteristic inputs together.
accepted.sec: Organic and natural inputs - vermicompost, green manure, NPOP, PKVY, ZBNF, APCNF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly states the coverage and target of APCNF?
o: It covers 4.89 lakh farmers on 10.20 lakh hectares and targets 19 lakh farmers on 41 lakh hectares by 2028–29.
It covers 41 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh hectares and targets 10.20 lakh farmers on 19 lakh hectares.
It covers 10.20 lakh farmers on 4.89 lakh hectares and targets 41 lakh farmers on 19 lakh hectares by 2028–29.
It covers 7 lakh farmers on 19 lakh hectares and targets 10.20 lakh farmers by 2028–29.
accepted.x: The stated APCNF coverage is 10.20 lakh farmers over 4.89 lakh hectares, with a target of 41 lakh farmers over 19 lakh hectares by 2028–29.
accepted.tq: Compare present coverage with future target while checking the farmer-area pairing.
accepted.sec: Organic and natural inputs - vermicompost, green manure, NPOP, PKVY, ZBNF, APCNF  [APPSC]

accepted.s: APCNF received which award for the year 2024?
o: Sardar Patel Outstanding ICAR Institute Award
World Food Prize for Seed Innovation

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding NMSA:
1. It is one of the eight missions under NAPCC.
2. It was merged into PM-RKVY from 2022–23.
3. Its components include Soil Health Management and the agroforestry sub-mission ‘Har Medh Par Ped’.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

accepted.s: What change occurred in Andhra Pradesh’s pesticide use between 2014–15 and 2024–25?
o: It fell from 39.39 LMT to 17.22 LMT of active ingredient.
It fell from 2,650 MT to 1,716 MT of active ingredient.
It remained unchanged at 2,650 MT of active ingredient.
It increased from 1,716 MT to 2,650 MT of active ingredient.
accepted.x: Pesticide use declined from 2,650 MT in 2014–15 to 1,716 MT in 2024–25, measured as active ingredient.
accepted.tq: Track the direction of change and retain the correct measurement unit.

accepted.s: Rythu Seva Kendras, formerly known as Rythu Bharosa Kendras, function primarily as:
o: Village-level one-stop centres for agricultural services
accepted.x: Rythu Seva Kendras are village one-stop centres providing a range of agricultural inputs and services.

accepted.s: Which of the following services is NOT associated with Rythu Seva Kendras?
accepted.x: RSKs handle inputs, soil testing, e-Panta, CCRCs, insurance and procurement. Approval of GM crops is associated with GEAC, not RSKs.

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly represents the rationalisation of soil-sampling centres in Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: Soil sampling initially ran through 10,778 RSKs; these were rationalised to 8,489 functional centres.

accepted.s: For 2026–27, AP Seeds is supplying subsidised seed through Rythu Seva Kendras in which combination?

7.46 lakh quintals at a cost of ₹294 crore
